UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    ```
    ```python
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of

```python

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1001想退货，请查一下
客服:亲，查到您的订单1001是无线耳机（299元），状态为已签收。签收后15天内支持无理由退货，商品需保持完好、吊牌和包装齐全且不影响二次销售[1]。如需办理，可以告诉我，我帮您转接人工客服跟进～
最新消息:抱歉我说错了，应该查订单1002，能不能取消？

tools.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
tools.title: ResolvedQuestion

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```
messages.title: SystemMessage

messages.description:
Message from the user.

A `HumanMessage` is a message that is passed in from a user to the model.

Example:

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of

```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

items.question: 签收后多久可以无理由退货？

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

messages.description:

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

```python

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1001想退货，请查一下
客服:订单1001（无线耳机，299元）状态为已签收，但订单信息里没有签收日期，我无法判断是否还在15天无理由退货窗口内，因此暂时不能确认这一单能否退货。若签收未超过15天且商品完好、吊牌包装齐全，一般可申请无理由退货[4]；建议您提供签收日期或转人工客服核实。
最新消息:抱歉我说错了，应该查订单1002，能不能取消？

tools.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
tools.title: ResolvedQuestion

parsed.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
parsed.title: ResolvedQuestion

raw.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
raw.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

    ```python
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]
    ```

```python
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```

按订单号查询订单的基础信息:商品、金额、状态;不包含物流轨迹。
用户问订单买了什么、多少钱、什么状态时使用;问包裹/物流到哪了时不要用本工具。
args_schema.title: query_order

args_schema.description: 语义检索常见问题知识库并精排。用户问退货政策、发货时间、邮费运费、付款、发票、会员等常见问题,或问具体商品型号(如 SH-E300)的参数、价格时使用;能从用户话里明确判断品类时传 category,判断不了不要传。

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall


!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

response.description: Message chunk from an AI (yielded when streaming).
response.title: AIMessageChunk

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

items.answer: 退货验收通过后，退款原路返回；微信或支付宝一般 1 到 3 个工作日到账，具体以支付渠道为准。

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

raw.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1002想退款，先看看状态
客服:亲，订单1002是机械键盘，金额399元，目前状态为「已发货」。退款方面，退货验收通过后款项会原路退回，微信或支付宝一般1到3个工作日到账，具体以支付渠道为准[1]。您可以在订单页提交退款申请，需要我帮您转人工协助处理吗？
最新消息:更正，是订单1003，还没发货，能取消吗？

tools.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
tools.title: ResolvedQuestion

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

按订单号查询订单的基础信息:商品、金额、状态;不包含物流轨迹。
        用户问订单买了什么、多少钱、什么状态时使用;问包裹/物流到哪了时不要用本工具。
tools.name: query_order

args_schema.description: 语义检索常见问题知识库并精排。用户问退货政策、发货时间、邮费运费、付款、发票、会员等常见问题,或问具体商品型号(如 SH-E300)的参数、价格时使用;能从用户话里明确判断品类时传 category,判断不了不要传。
args_schema.title: query_faq

tools.description: 语义检索常见问题知识库并精排。用户问退货政策、发货时间、邮费运费、付款、发票、会员等常见问题,或问具体商品型号(如 SH-E300)的参数、价格时使用;能从用户话里明确判断品类时传 category,判断不了不要传。
tools.name: query_faq

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1002想退款，先看看状态
客服:订单1002是机械键盘，金额399元，目前状态为「已发货」[4]。按政策，商品签收后15天内可无理由退货，需保持完好、吊牌包装齐全[4]；退货验收通过后原路退款，微信或支付宝一般1到3个工作日到账[5]。由于系统未记录签收日期，能否退还需以实际签收时间判断，建议您转人工客服核实。
最新消息:更正，是订单1003，还没发货，能取消吗？

tools.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
tools.title: ResolvedQuestion

parsed.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
parsed.title: ResolvedQuestion

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

messages.description:

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1001退款进度请查一下
客服:【无法回答】抱歉，订单1001目前显示为「已签收」，我这边查不到退款进度信息，建议您转人工客服核实处理。
最新消息:不退了，只查订单1002状态

tools.title: ResolvedQuestion

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of

```python

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of

```python

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,

        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,

        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

    used by the LangSmith platform.

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata
