When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;

`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

response.description: Message chunk from an AI (yielded when streaming).
response.title: AIMessageChunk

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

    ```python
    ]
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1002可以取消吗？
客服:亲，您的订单1002（机械键盘，399元）目前是已发货状态，不能直接取消哦[1]。您可以拒收包裹，或签收后申请退货[1]；需要我帮您转人工进一步处理吗？
最新消息:我改口了，想问未发货取消规则

tools.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
tools.title: ResolvedQuestion

parsed.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
parsed.title: ResolvedQuestion

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

A `HumanMessage` is a message that is passed in from a user to the model.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Instantiate a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    model = ...
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:

    ```python
        "cache_read": 100,
    ```

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

of input messages.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。

response.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

    ```python
    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1001要退款
客服:亲，查到订单1001是无线耳机（299元），状态为已签收，可以申请退货退款哦。退货验收通过后，退款会原路返回，微信或支付宝一般1到3个工作日到账，具体以支付渠道为准[1]。需要我帮您转人工客服发起退货申请吗？
最新消息:我不要退款了，想换货，查订单1003

tools.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
tools.title: ResolvedQuestion

parsed.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
parsed.title: ResolvedQuestion

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

A `HumanMessage` is a message that is passed in from a user to the model.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Instantiate a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    model = ...
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```
messages.title: HumanMessage

args_schema.description:
按订单号查询订单的基础信息:商品、金额、状态;不包含物流轨迹。
用户问订单买了什么、多少钱、什么状态时使用;问包裹/物流到哪了时不要用本工具。

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1001要退款
客服:亲，订单1001（无线耳机，299元）状态为已签收，签收后15天内可无理由退货，商品需保持完好、吊牌包装齐全[1]。退货验收通过后原路退款，微信或支付宝一般1到3个工作日到账[2]。如需发起退货，我可以帮您转接人工客服处理哦～
最新消息:我不要退款了，想换货，查订单1003

tools.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。

InputTokenDetails.description:

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

raw.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```
messages.title: SystemMessage

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:帮我查订单1001的退货流程
客服:亲，订单1001是无线耳机（299元），状态为已签收。签收后15天内支持无理由退货，商品需保持完好、吊牌和包装齐全，不影响二次销售[1]。具体退货入口和寄回方式我这边查不到，建议您转人工客服协助办理哦～
最新消息:单号错了，是订单9999

tools.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
tools.title: ResolvedQuestion

parsed.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
parsed.title: ResolvedQuestion

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

    used by the LangSmith platform.

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:帮我查订单1001的退货流程
客服:订单1001是无线耳机，金额299元，状态为已签收。签收后15天内支持无理由退货，商品需保持完好、吊牌和包装齐全，不影响二次销售[1]。退货验收通过后，退款会原路返回，微信或支付宝一般1到3个工作日到账[3]。
最新消息:单号错了，是订单9999

tools.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
tools.title: ResolvedQuestion

raw.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:

ToolCallChunk.description:

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,

        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,

        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

    used by the LangSmith platform.

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1001的状态是什么？
客服:亲，订单1001（无线耳机，299元）目前状态是「已签收」哦～还有其他需要帮忙的吗？
最新消息:改查订单1003，还没发货吧？

tools.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
tools.title: ResolvedQuestion

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
