messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:

of input messages.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    ```
    ```python
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    ```python
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    ```
    ```python
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

response.description: Message chunk from an AI (yielded when streaming).
response.title: AIMessageChunk

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1001的状态是什么？
客服:亲，订单1001（无线耳机，299元）目前状态是「已签收」哦～还有其他需要帮忙的吗？
最新消息:改查订单1003，还没发货吧？

tools.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
tools.title: ResolvedQuestion

the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    ```
    ```python
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

of input messages.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    ```
    ```python
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    ```
    ```python
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    ```
    ```python
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

```python
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    ```
    ```python
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1001退款能多久到账？
客服:亲，订单1001（无线耳机，299元）目前状态是已签收。退货验收通过后，退款会原路返回；微信或支付宝一般1到3个工作日到账，具体以支付渠道为准[1]。具体到账时间无法承诺，建议您留意支付渠道通知哦～
最新消息:算了，我只想知道银行卡最长多久

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of

```python

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ```

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of

```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

用户问订单买了什么、多少钱、什么状态时使用;问包裹/物流到哪了时不要用本工具。
args_schema.title: query_order

tools.description:
按订单号查询订单的基础信息:商品、金额、状态;不包含物流轨迹。
        用户问订单买了什么、多少钱、什么状态时使用;问包裹/物流到哪了时不要用本工具。
tools.name: query_order

args_schema.description: 语义检索常见问题知识库并精排。用户问退货政策、发货时间、邮费运费、付款、发票、会员等常见问题,或问具体商品型号(如 SH-E300)的参数、价格时使用;能从用户话里明确判断品类时传 category,判断不了不要传。
args_schema.title: query_faq

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1001退款能多久到账？
客服:订单1001（无线耳机，299元）目前状态为已签收，退货验收通过后，退款会原路返回；微信或支付宝一般 1 到 3 个工作日到账，具体以支付渠道为准 [3]。另外，签收后 15 天内支持无理由退货，商品需保持完好、吊牌和包装齐全 [2]。
最新消息:算了，我只想知道银行卡最长多久

```python
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

    ```python
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:我想退货，暂时没找到订单号
客服:您好，退货需要先定位订单，麻烦您提供订单号或下单手机号，我帮您查一下～
最新消息:找到了，是订单1001，商品已签收；还在15天退货期内吗？

```python
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(

    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

response.description: Message chunk from an AI (yielded when streaming).
response.title: AIMessageChunk

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

of input messages.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

items.answer: 无理由退货需在适用时限内发起，商品保持完好，吊牌和包装齐全，并且不影响二次销售。
items.question: 无理由退货需要满足什么条件？
items.section_path: CH15 模拟政策 > 退货条件

items.answer: 退货验收通过后，退款原路返回；微信或支付宝一般 1 到 3 个工作日到账，具体以支付渠道为准。
items.question: 退货验收后多久退款？

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

raw.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of

```python

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of

```python

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of

```python

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1002已发货，我想退款
客服:亲，您的订单1002（机械键盘，399元）目前是已发货状态，已发货订单不能直接取消退款，可以拒收包裹，或签收后申请退货 [2]。退货验收通过后款项原路退回，微信或支付宝一般1到3个工作日到账，具体以支付渠道为准 [1]。需要我帮您转人工协助办理吗？
最新消息:更正，想查订单1003能否取消

tools.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
tools.title: ResolvedQuestion

parsed.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
parsed.title: ResolvedQuestion

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1002已发货，我想退款
客服:您好，订单1002（机械键盘，399元）目前状态为已发货，已发货订单不能直接取消，您可以拒收，或签收后申请退货 [3]；签收后15天内支持无理由退货，商品需保持完好、吊牌包装齐全 [2]。
最新消息:更正，想查订单1003能否取消

ToolCallChunk.description:

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

messages.description:

of input messages.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of

```python

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1001我想退货
客服:您好，订单1001是无线耳机（299元），状态为已签收。签收后15天内支持无理由退货，商品需保持完好、吊牌和包装齐全且不影响二次销售[1]。您方便说下签收日期吗？我帮您确认是否还在退货窗口内～
最新消息:撤回申请，我不退了，也不要建工单

tools.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
tools.title: ResolvedQuestion

parsed.description: ch06 指代消解+改写:resolved 为补全后完整问法;changed=false 表示原样透传。
parsed.title: ResolvedQuestion

Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata
