This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

response.description: Message chunk from an AI (yielded when streaming).
response.title: AIMessageChunk

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

messages.description:

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    ```
    ```python
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    ```
    ```python
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

response.title: AIMessageChunk

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,

        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,

        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

    used by the LangSmith platform.

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1001我想退货
客服:亲，订单1001（无线耳机，299元）目前状态是已签收，下单时间为2026-08-30。按政策，签收后15天内可无理由退货，商品需保持完好、吊牌和包装齐全，不影响二次销售[3]；退货验收通过后原路退款，微信或支付宝一般1到3个工作日到账[4]。不过系统里查不到您的签收日期，无法确认是否还在15天窗口内，建议您转人工客服核实后再提交退货申请哦～
最新消息:撤回申请，我不退了，也不要建工单

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message from the user.

A `HumanMessage` is a message that is passed in from a user to the model.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Instantiate a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    model = ...
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```
messages.title: HumanMessage

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:

of input messages.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1001申请退货，需要保留什么？
客服:亲，订单1001（无线耳机，299元，已签收）申请退货时，请保持商品完好，吊牌和包装齐全，不影响二次销售 [1]；签收后15天内可发起无理由退货 [2]。
最新消息:我改问运费，非质量问题谁承担？

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```
messages.title: SystemMessage

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of

```python

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

response.description: Message chunk from an AI (yielded when streaming).
response.title: AIMessageChunk

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

request.messages:
你是电商客服的问法澄清器。根据对话历史处理用户最新消息:
1. 消息里有代词或省略指代(它、这个、上面那单等)时,结合历史把指代替换成具体对象,补全成不看历史也能看懂的完整问题;
2. 口语、模糊的问法改写成规范问法;
3. 消息本身已完整、指代明确时,原样返回且 changed 取 false;
只依据历史里出现过的事实补全,不新增假设;changed 取 true 表示你改写过。只输出两个字段:resolved(字符串)、changed(布尔)。
对话历史:
【早期对话梗概】(无)
【最近对话】
用户:订单1001申请退货，需要保留什么？
客服:订单1001（无线耳机，299元）目前状态为已签收，可以申请无理由退货，但需要满足以下条件：商品保持完好，吊牌和包装齐全，并且不影响二次销售[4]；同时，需要在签收后15天内发起退货[5]。建议您保留好原包装、吊牌和配件，方便后续验收。
最新消息:我改问运费，非质量问题谁承担？

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

tools.name: query_faq

InputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

messages.description:

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,

        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,

        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

    used by the LangSmith platform.

    ```python
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

    ```python
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,

        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,

        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

    used by the LangSmith platform.

messages.description:

    ```python
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```
