Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

items.answer: 未发货订单可申请取消并原路退款；已发货订单不能直接取消，可拒收或签收后申请退货。

items.answer: 退货验收通过后，退款原路返回；微信或支付宝一般 1 到 3 个工作日到账，具体以支付渠道为准。
items.question: 退货验收后多久退款？

raw.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
raw.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of

```python

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:

```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(

    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

Message from an AI.

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
InputTokenDetails.title: InputTokenDetails

InvalidToolCall.description:
Allowance for errors made by LLM.

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

raw.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
raw.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

response.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

Breakdown of input token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full input token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "cache_creation": 200,
        "cache_read": 100,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Instantiate a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    model = ...
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of

```python

right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

resolved_messages: 订单1002已发货，退货能否直接当作取消？

arguments.keyword: 已发货订单能否取消，退货与取消的区别

items.answer: 未发货订单可申请取消并原路退款；已发货订单不能直接取消，可拒收或签收后申请退货。
items.question: 订单发货前后如何取消？

items.answer: 2026-06-01 起，商品签收后 15 天内支持无理由退货；商品需保持完好，吊牌和包装齐全，不影响二次销售。
items.question: 签收后多久可以无理由退货？
items.section_path: CH15 模拟政策 > 无理由退货窗口

items.answer: 未发货订单可申请取消并原路退款；已发货订单不能直接取消，可拒收或签收后申请退货。
items.question: 订单发货前后如何取消？
items.section_path: CH15 模拟政策 > 订单取消

items.answer: 2026-06-01 起，商品签收后 15 天内支持无理由退货；商品需保持完好，吊牌和包装齐全，不影响二次销售。
items.question: 签收后多久可以无理由退货？
items.section_path: CH15 模拟政策 > 无理由退货窗口

items.answer: 退货验收通过后，退款原路返回；微信或支付宝一般 1 到 3 个工作日到账，具体以支付渠道为准。

ToolCall.description:

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

raw.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
raw.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```
messages.title: ToolMessage

Here we add an `error` key to surface errors made during generation
(e.g., invalid JSON arguments.)
InvalidToolCall.title: InvalidToolCall

OutputTokenDetails.description:
Breakdown of output token counts.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"
OutputTokenDetails.title: OutputTokenDetails

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:
Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

messages.description:
Message from an AI.

An `AIMessage` is returned from a chat model as a response to a prompt.

This message represents the output of the model and consists of both
the raw output as returned by the model and standardized fields
(e.g., tool calls, usage metadata) added by the LangChain framework.
messages.title: AIMessage

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,

messages.description:
Message for passing the result of executing a tool back to a model.

`ToolMessage` objects contain the result of a tool invocation. Typically, the result
is encoded inside the `content` field.

`tool_call_id` is used to associate the tool call request with the tool call
response. Useful in situations where a chat model is able to request multiple tool
calls in parallel.

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` representing a result of `42` from a tool call with id

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    ToolMessage(content="42", tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL")
    ```

Example:
    A `ToolMessage` where only part of the tool output is sent to the model
    and the full output is passed in to artifact.

    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

    tool_output = {
        "stdout": "From the graph we can see that the correlation between "
        "x and y is ...",
        "stderr": None,
        "artifacts": {"type": "image", "base64_data": "/9j/4gIcSU..."},
    }

    ToolMessage(
        content=tool_output["stdout"],
        artifact=tool_output,
        tool_call_id="call_Jja7J89XsjrOLA5r!MEOW!SL",
    )
    ```

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

UsageMetadata.description:

Example:
    ```python

        "input_tokens": 350,

        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.

Does *not* need to sum to full output token count. Does *not* need to have all keys.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "audio": 10,
        "reasoning": 200,
    }
    ```

May also hold extra provider-specific keys.

!!! version-added "Added in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python
    {"name": "foo", "args": {"a": 1}, "id": "123"}
    ```

    This represents a request to call the tool named `'foo'` with arguments
    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

!!! note "Factory function"

    `tool_call` may also be used as a factory to create a `ToolCall`. Benefits
    include:

    * Required arguments strictly validated at creation time
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```
ToolCallChunk.title: ToolCallChunk

Usage metadata for a message, such as token counts.

This is a standard representation of token usage that is consistent across models.

Example:
    ```python
    {
        "input_tokens": 350,
        "output_tokens": 240,
        "total_tokens": 590,
        "input_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "cache_creation": 200,
            "cache_read": 100,
        },
        "output_token_details": {
            "audio": 10,
            "reasoning": 200,
        },
    }
    ```

!!! warning "Behavior changed in `langchain-core` 0.3.9"

    Added `input_token_details` and `output_token_details`.

!!! note "LangSmith SDK"

    The LangSmith SDK also has a `UsageMetadata` class. While the two share fields,
    LangSmith's `UsageMetadata` has additional fields to capture cost information
    used by the LangSmith platform.
UsageMetadata.title: UsageMetadata

ToolCall.description:
Represents an AI's request to call a tool.

Example:
    ```python

    `{"a": 1}` and an identifier of `'123'`.

    include:

ToolCallChunk.description:
A chunk of a tool call (yielded when streaming).

When merging `ToolCallChunk` objects (e.g., via `AIMessageChunk.__add__`), all
string attributes are concatenated. Chunks are only merged if their values of
`index` are equal and not `None`.

Example:
```python
left_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":', index=0)]
right_chunks = [ToolCallChunk(name=None, args="1}", index=0)]

(
    AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=left_chunks)
    + AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=right_chunks)
).tool_call_chunks == [ToolCallChunk(name="foo", args='{"a":1}', index=0)]
```

messages.description:
Message for priming AI behavior.

The system message is usually passed in as the first of a sequence
of input messages.

Example:
    ```python
    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

    messages = [
        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```

    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

        SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant! Your name is Bob."),
        HumanMessage(content="What is your name?"),
    ]

    # Define a chat model and invoke it with the messages
    print(model.invoke(messages))
    ```
